study_identification_part.si4_title: Microstructural mapping of neural pathways in Alzheimer's disease using macrostructure-informed normative tractometry

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat harmonization was used. It was applied bundle-wise for 9 features (5 MAE, 4 DTI). Age and sex were preserved as covariates. ComBat parameters were estimated on a training set of CN subjects and applied to the test set to prevent data leakage.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Along-tract bundle profiles for all nine features were harmonized using ComBat using the bundle-wise approach described in Chandio et al. 15 ComBat is a 'location and scale' model...Covariates can also be specified in ComBat to preserve the known biological variability across subjects (eg, age and sex). In this study, ComBat was run for each of the 30 bundles and nine features, by pooling information across 100 segments of each bundle, with age and sex modeled as covariates...To prevent data leakage, 54,55 we estimated ComBat parameters on bundle profiles created from the training set for both cohorts previously used in fine-tuning...The estimated ComBat parameters were then applied to bundle profiles from the test set...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: A linear regression model was used to assess group differences (MCI vs CN, Dementia vs CN) in the 9 diffusion measures, with age and sex as covariates. For merged cohort analysis, a linear mixed model was used with cohort as a random effect. Partial Spearman rank-order correlation was used to associate bundle-averaged diffusion measures with clinical scores (CDRsb, ADAS13, MMSE, WLDR, SMIR, SMDR), controlling for age and sex. Multiple comparisons were corrected using FDR.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: In two diverse cohorts, the proposed MINT framework identified consistent and widespread WM diffusivity abnormalities in MCI and dementia, particularly in temporal and posterior regions, and helped to disentangle microstructural changes from macrostructural alterations, especially for the FA metric.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study introduced MINT, a multivariate normative model, to map WM changes in 1032 subjects from US (ADNI) and Indian (NIMHANS) cohorts. Widespread effects of MCI and dementia were found, with increased diffusivity (MD, RD, AxD) and altered geometry (MAE-Shape), particularly in temporal lobe tracts (ILF, UF, AF) and the corpus callosum. Findings were consistent across cohorts, though with stronger statistical significance in the larger ADNI sample. MD and RD were the most sensitive DTI metrics to dementia. MINT helped interpret paradoxical FA findings in projection pathways, showing that these were highly correlated with macrostructural changes (MAE-Shape), suggesting that fiber crossings confound traditional DTI analysis. MINT-derived measures showed comparable or stronger associations with clinical severity scores (CDRsb, WLDR) than standard DTI metrics.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Tractography and segmentation methods can fail, particularly for certain bundles (e.g., fornix, cingulum, UF, IFOF), which might affect downstream analysis. The use of DTI metrics (FA, RD, AxD) has inherent limitations in areas with crossing fibers. Differences in demographics, sample size, and clinical assessment protocols between the ADNI and NIMHANS cohorts could confound cross-cohort comparisons.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Even among the 30 bundles we used in this study, UF and IFOF bundles were not well reconstructed in all subjects across all protocols, which might have affected downstream harmonization and statistical analysis (Section S5)... Although multisite data can be harmonized across scanners and protocols, we analyzed ADNI and NIMHANS data separately because participants in these two cohorts were recruited from different geographic regions and had very different demographics. Cognitive assessments conducted in different languages were not harmonized prior to diagnosis.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study uses a transfer learning approach, pre-training a VAE on a large external dataset (TractoInferno) and then fine-tuning it on smaller, site-specific healthy control groups. This demonstrates a practical application for multi-site studies where raw data sharing is restricted. The MINT framework produces five deviation scores (MAE-Shape, MAE-FA, etc.) plus the four traditional DTI metrics, allowing for a richer, multi-faceted analysis of white matter pathology.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study provides a compelling demonstration of using a deep generative model (VAE) as a normative model for tractography data. A key innovation is the joint modeling of microstructure (DTI metrics) and macrostructure (fiber geometry), which helps to disambiguate findings from metrics like FA that are sensitive to crossing fibers. The validation across two distinct cohorts (North American and Indian) strengthens the generalizability of the findings and the utility of the MINT framework. The code and pre-trained model are publicly available.
